title: CVE-2026-107929: local interface connection reuse mixup
excerpt:
## Summary:

When CURLOPT_INTERFACE is set with one of the documented prefixes (`if!`, `host!`, `ifhost!`), that binding is not part of the connection reuse key, so a later transfer asking for a different source can silently reuse an existing connection and go out from the earlier transfer's source address. `Curl_parse_interface()` parses the option into three separate values and `setstropt_interface()` stores them as STRING_DEVICE, STRING_INTERFACE and STRING_BINDHOST (lib/cf-socket.c:588, lib/setopt.c:155-183), and `bindlocal()` uses all three (lib/cf-socket.c:661-663), but `allocate_conn()` copies only STRING_DEVICE into `conn->localdev` (lib/url.c:1208-1209) and the local-binding test in `url_match_connect_config()` compares only that field and the local ports (lib/url.c:625-628). The unprefixed form is unaffected because it lands in STRING_DEVICE and is already in the key, which is why the control below behaves correctly. Reuse never rebinds a socket, so the second transfer keeps the first connection's source address, and for the same reason a non-matching `if!` skips the CURLE_INTERFACE_FAILED that CURLOPT_INTERFACE(3) documents. I know the comment at lib/url.c:619-624 calls this matching deliberately rough, but it assumes reuse will "reuse the exact same binding parameters", and here they are explicitly different and the miss goes in the unsafe direction.

## Affected version

8.9.0 through 8.22.0, and current master. I reproduced it on released 8.22.0 and on master efd42dfbbf656870f8885815d07b0d16a5771f69. On master 424aa994ac223c0f90839aadee0fb59595344fce I only read the source: `allocate_conn()` has moved to url.c:1147 but still copies STRING_DEVICE alone, and STRING_INTERFACE and STRING_BINDHOST are still read nowhere but the bind path. The 8.9.0 lower bound comes from reading commit 3060557af702dd59155ea703a0790455c2f49a59, which split the option into three strings without adding the two new ones to the reuse key; I did not run 8.9.0.

```
curl 8.22.0 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.22.0 OpenSSL/3.0.13 zlib/1.3 zstd/1.5.5
Release-Date: 2026-09-02
```

Linux 6.8.0 x86_64, clang 18.1.3, built from the signed 8.22.0 release tarball. That build was configured with --enable-debug; the code above is not debug-conditional.

## Steps To Reproduce:

The server has to speak HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, otherwise nothing is reusable and the bug stays hidden. Minima

key_reasons: The code confirms that CURLOPT_INTERFACE with prefixes (if!, host!, ifhost!) is parsed into three separate strings (STRING_DEVICE, STRING_INTERFACE, STRING_BINDHOST) but only STRING_DEVICE is stored in the connection struct (conn->localdev) and compared during connection reuse.
bindlocal() reads all three strings when initially binding a socket, but connection reuse skips rebinding, so the second request's different source binding is silently ignored.
The unprefixed form works correctly because it lands entirely in STRING_DEVICE, which is already in the reuse key.
This allows a multi-tenant application sharing a libcurl connection cache to have one tenant's traffic egress from another tenant's source IP, bypassing source-IP ACLs.
The flaw exists in both the tested release (8.22.0) and current master (efd42dfb).
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and reproduction. The code confirms the flaw: CURLOPT_INTERFACE with prefixes (if!, host!, ifhost!) is parsed into three strings but only STRING_DEVICE enters the connection reuse key (lib/url.c:1139-1142, lib/url.c:624-628). On reuse, bindlocal() is not called, so the second request's different binding is ignored. This is a valid security issue for applications using per-tenant source bindings with a shared connection cache. We will prepare a fix that includes STRING_INTERFACE and STRING_BINDHOST in the reuse key. Your patch approach of rebuilding the full spelling into localdev is sound; please open a PR when ready.
